CHAPTER V. After the kingdoms of Spain, the Carthaginians were the first to occupy the empire of the province. For when the Gaditani, at the command of a dream, had transferred the sacred rites of Hercules from Tyre—whence the Carthaginians also trace their origin—to Spain and had founded a city there, the neighboring peoples of Spain envied the growth of the new city and, for that reason, harassed the Gaditani with war. The Carthaginians sent aid to their kinsmen. In a successful expedition, they both vindicated the Gaditani from injury and added the greater part of the province to their own empire. Later, encouraged by the auspices of the first expedition, they sent the commander Hamilcar with a great force to occupy the province. After achieving great things, while Fortune followed him too incautiously, he was led into an ambush and killed. His son-in-law, Hasdrubal, was sent into his place, and he too was killed by a slave of a certain Spaniard, who was avenging the unjust death of his own master. Hannibal, the son of Hamilcar—greater than either of them—succeeded him. Having surpassed the deeds of both, he subdued all of Spain. From there, having brought war upon the Romans, he exhausted Italy for sixteen years with various disasters. Meanwhile, the Romans sent the Scipios into Spain, who first drove the Carthaginians from the province and later waged grave wars against the Spaniards themselves. Nor could the yoke of Spain be accepted by the province until Caesar Augustus, having subdued the world, transferred his victorious arms to them and, having led the barbarous and fierce people to a more cultivated habit of life through laws, reduced the region to the form of a province.

### Scincus. What is it? <note>original: "Sı̄ncus"; referring to the Skink, a type of lizard</note>
It is an aquatic animal captured on the banks of the Nile. It is said to be a land-dwelling creature, for when it comes out of the water, it takes the form of a living animal <note>Medieval naturalists often categorized the skink as a "land crocodile" or a hybrid of fish and lizard</note>. **Selection.** The best kind is that which is captured in the spring and in places where they are fervent for mating. The larger it is, the better; the fatter it is, the better. Its fat should be taken with honey. **Instruments of the Joints.** It benefits cold diseases of the joints. **Organs of Expulsion.** Its salt excites sexual intercourse, but its flesh does so even more. Indeed, the flesh of this animal, specifically the parts near the kidneys and their fat, is used as an aphrodisiac.

### Spinach <note>original: "Pinacha"; from the Arabic 'isbanakh'</note>. 
**Nature.** It is cold and moist at the end of the first degree. **Operations and Properties.** It is softening and its nutrition is better for the body when it is well-digested. I say that its juice is [unclear], it washes the [unclear] and benefits the bile. It is eaten for its juice. **Organs of Breath and Chest.** It benefits breathing, the chest, and a hot lung. **Instruments of the Joints.** It is used for pains of the back caused by the blood. **Organs of Expulsion.** It is softening for the belly <note>meaning it acts as a mild laxative</note>.

### Flaxseed <note>original: "Semen lini"</note>. 
What is it? It is the primary companion to fenugreek. **Nature.** It is hot in the first degree, balanced in moisture and dryness. It is said that there is a great deal of superfluous moisture in it. **Operations and Properties.** It is maturing <note>it helps ripen abscesses or boils</note>, and it cleanses through its superfluous moisture. From it, that which is made [unclear] has a clear and balanced astringency in its essence. It is declared to be softening and a sedative for pain, much like chamomile. **Beauty.** From it, a plaster is made for the skin and nails. It benefits the [unclear] of the nails, cracks, and...
